evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CapZ regulates spindle assembly during mitosis independent of actin assembly.
source: Interestingly, CapZ has also been reported to regulate spindle assembly during mitosis independent of actin assembly (di Pietro et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CapZ docks to endocytic vesicles via its C-terminal actin-binding motif.
source: Here, we found that CapZ docks to endocytic vesicles via its C-terminal actin-binding motif.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding from the current study and supported by experimental data.

claim: CapZβ knockout changed cell morphology.
source: Similar to the previous study by Sinnar et al., 2014, CapZβ knockout in HeLa cells changed cell morphology and inhibited cell migration (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B and cites previous work.

claim: CapZβ knockout inhibited cell migration.
source: Similar to the previous study by Sinnar et al., 2014, CapZβ knockout in HeLa cells changed cell morphology and inhibited cell migration (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B and cites previous work.

claim: CapZβ knockout increased cell size.
source: CapZβ knockout also increased cell size (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: After EGF binds to its receptors (EGFR), the receptor complex was internalized normally in control, CapZβ-knockout, and CapZβ-reconstituted cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D, after EGF binds to its receptors (EGFR), the receptor complex was internalized normally in control, CapZβ-knockout, and CapZβ-reconstituted cells, but its degradation was significantly inhibited in CapZβ-knockout cells when compared to the control cells and CapZβ-reconstituted cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: EGFR degradation was significantly inhibited in CapZβ-knockout cells when compared to the control cells and CapZβ-reconstituted cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D, after EGF binds to its receptors (EGFR), the receptor complex was internalized normally in control, CapZβ-knockout, and CapZβ-reconstituted cells, but its degradation was significantly inhibited in CapZβ-knockout cells when compared to the control cells and CapZβ-reconstituted cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: EGF treatment triggered EGFR degradation in control cells.
source: We showed that EGF treatment triggered EGFR degradation in control cells, yet its degradation in CapZβ-knockout cells was inhibited (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: EGFR degradation in CapZβ-knockout cells was inhibited.
source: We showed that EGF treatment triggered EGFR degradation in control cells, yet its degradation in CapZβ-knockout cells was inhibited (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The basal level of EGFR protein in CapZβ-knockout cells was lower than in control cells.
source: Of note, the basal level of EGFR protein or mRNA in CapZβ-knockout cells was lower than in control cells, and reconstituting CapZβ restored the expression of EGFR (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F–1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F–1G.

claim: The basal level of EGFR mRNA in CapZβ-knockout cells was lower than in control cells.
source: Of note, the basal level of EGFR protein or mRNA in CapZβ-knockout cells was lower than in control cells, and reconstituting CapZβ restored the expression of EGFR (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F–1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F–1G.

claim: Reconstituting CapZβ restored the expression of EGFR.
source: Of note, the basal level of EGFR protein or mRNA in CapZβ-knockout cells was lower than in control cells, and reconstituting CapZβ restored the expression of EGFR (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F–1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F–1G.

claim: CapZ or F-actin dynamics positively regulate the transcription of EGFR.
source: This result suggests that CapZ or F-actin dynamics positively regulate the transcription of EGFR.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that EGFR expression is reduced in CapZβ-knockout cells.

claim: Actin dynamics have been shown to modulate gene transcription.
source: Along this line, actin dynamics have been shown to modulate gene transcription (Olson and Nordheim, 2010; Knöll, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CapZβ knockout significantly inhibited transferrin recycling.
source: We showed that CapZβ knockout significantly inhibited transferrin recycling (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H), suggesting that CapZ might be involved in the fast recycling from the early endosome or RAB11-positive recycling endosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claim: CapZ might be involved in the fast recycling from the early endosome or RAB11-positive recycling endosomes.
source: We showed that CapZβ knockout significantly inhibited transferrin recycling (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H), suggesting that CapZ might be involved in the fast recycling from the early endosome or RAB11-positive recycling endosomes.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the transferrin recycling data.

claim: Fluorescent transferrin labeling was reduced in CapZβ-knockout cells.
source: Of note, fluorescent transferrin labeling was reduced in CapZβ-knockout cells, which might be due to the decreased expression levels of TfR in CapZβ-knockout cells.
evidence: The claim is based on observation from the transferrin recycling assay.

claim: The reduced fluorescent transferrin labeling in CapZβ-knockout cells might be due to the decreased expression levels of TfR.
source: Of note, fluorescent transferrin labeling was reduced in CapZβ-knockout cells, which might be due to the decreased expression levels of TfR in CapZβ-knockout cells.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on inference.

claim: CapZ participates in endocytosis after the internalization of endocytic vesicles.
source: In summary, these results indicate that CapZ participates in endocytosis after the internalization of endocytic vesicles.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the EGFR degradation and transferrin recycling assays.

claim: EGFR-containing endocytic vesicles in CapZβ-knockout cells appear to be smaller and more abundant when compared to the control cells.
source: Since EGFR-containing endocytic vesicles in CapZβ-knockout cells appear to be smaller and more abundant when compared to the control cells (Figure 2B and C), we next examined whether the association of CapZ with endosomes is required for the maturation of early endosomes by comparing the size and the number of endosomes in CapZβ-knockout cells with the same parameters in control cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: The size of the RAB5-positive early endosomes was much smaller in the CapZβ-knockout cells than in the control cells.
source: We showed that the size of the RAB5-positive early endosomes was much smaller, whereas the number of endosomes was significantly higher in the CapZβ-knockout cells than in the control cells (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1I.

claim: The number of endosomes was significantly higher in the CapZβ-knockout cells than in the control cells.
source: We showed that the size of the RAB5-positive early endosomes was much smaller, whereas the number of endosomes was significantly higher in the CapZβ-knockout cells than in the control cells (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Addback of CapZβ to CapZβ-knockout HeLa cells restored the size and number of early endosomes to those in control cells.
source: Addback of CapZβ to CapZβ-knockout HeLa cells restored the size and number of early endosomes to those in control cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The fusion of small endocytic vesicles in the CapZβ-knockout cells is blocked or inhibited.
source: This suggests that the fusion of small endocytic vesicles in the CapZβ-knockout cells is blocked or inhibited.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of smaller and more numerous endosomes in CapZβ-knockout cells.

claim: CapZβ knockout exhibited a similar endosomal phenotype to that of RAB5-S34N overexpression.
source: Since CapZβ knockout exhibited a similar endosomal phenotype to that of RAB5-S34N overexpression (a GDP-bound dominant-negative mutant, RAB5 inactive form) (Galperin and Sorkin, 2003), we examined whether CapZβ knockout might impair the RAB5 activity by a GST-R5BD pulldown assay, in which the RAB5-binding domain (R5BD) of the RAB effector Rabaptin-5 specifically binds to GTP-bound RAB5.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison with previous work and supported by citation.

claim: RAB5-S34N is a GDP-bound dominant-negative mutant, RAB5 inactive form.
source: Since CapZβ knockout exhibited a similar endosomal phenotype to that of RAB5-S34N overexpression (a GDP-bound dominant-negative mutant, RAB5 inactive form) (Galperin and Sorkin, 2003), we examined whether CapZβ knockout might impair the RAB5 activity by a GST-R5BD pulldown assay, in which the RAB5-binding domain (R5BD) of the RAB effector Rabaptin-5 specifically binds to GTP-bound RAB5.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The level of RAB5-GTP was significantly lower in the CapZβ-knockout cells than that in the control cells.
source: We showed that the level of RAB5-GTP was significantly lower in the CapZβ-knockout cells than that in the control cells (Figure 2E), indicating that RAB5 is less active in the knockout cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by GST-R5BD pulldown assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: RAB5 is less active in the CapZβ-knockout cells.
source: We showed that the level of RAB5-GTP was significantly lower in the CapZβ-knockout cells than that in the control cells (Figure 2E), indicating that RAB5 is less active in the knockout cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the RAB5-GTP level data.

claim: CapZ participates in early endosome maturation.
source: In summary, these results indicate that CapZ participates in early endosome maturation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion from the experimental data on endosome size, number, and RAB5 activity.

claim: In CapZβ-knockout cells, the amount of F-actin was significantly increased.
source: As expected, in CapZβ-knockout cells, the amount of F-actin was significantly increased, and CapZβ-addack brought it down to the basal levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CapZβ-addback brought F-actin levels down to the basal levels.
source: As expected, in CapZβ-knockout cells, the amount of F-actin was significantly increased, and CapZβ-addack brought it down to the basal levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CapZα1/2 knockout significantly increased the amount of F-actin.
source: Similar to CapZβ knockout, CapZα1/2 knockout significantly increased the amount of F-actin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), and induced the accumulation of small early endosomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CapZα1/2 knockout induced the accumulation of small early endosomes.
source: Similar to CapZβ knockout, CapZα1/2 knockout significantly increased the amount of F-actin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), and induced the accumulation of small early endosomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by endosome analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Overexpression of both CapZα1-EGFP and CapZβ-mCherry in HeLa cells significantly decreased F-actin levels when compared to EGFP-mCherry-expressing cells.
source: On the other hand, overexpression of both CapZα1-EGFP and CapZβ-mCherry in HeLa cells significantly decreased F-actin levels when compared to EGFP-mCherry-expressing cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The size of RAB5-positive early endosomes was larger in the CapZ-overexpressing cells than in the EGFP-mCherry-expressing cells.
source: Consistently, the size of RAB5-positive early endosomes was larger, whereas the number of endosomes was lower in the CapZ-overexpressing cells than in the EGFP-mCherry-expressing cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by endosome analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The number of endosomes was lower in the CapZ-overexpressing cells than in the EGFP-mCherry-expressing cells.
source: Consistently, the size of RAB5-positive early endosomes was larger, whereas the number of endosomes was lower in the CapZ-overexpressing cells than in the EGFP-mCherry-expressing cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by endosome analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Latrunculin A markedly decreased the F-actin levels in control HeLa cells.
source: Latrunculin A markedly decreased the F-actin levels in control HeLa cells and was also able to revert the F-actin to basal levels in CapZβ-knockout HeLa cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Latrunculin A was able to revert the F-actin to basal levels in CapZβ-knockout HeLa cells.
source: Latrunculin A markedly decreased the F-actin levels in control HeLa cells and was also able to revert the F-actin to basal levels in CapZβ-knockout HeLa cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by phalloidin staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Latrunculin A increased the size of early endosomes in control cells.
source: Likewise, latrunculin A not only increased the size and decreased the number of early endosomes in control cells, but also partially rescued the defects of early endosomes in CapZβ-knockout cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).

claim: Latrunculin A decreased the number of early endosomes in control cells.
source: Likewise, latrunculin A not only increased the size and decreased the number of early endosomes in control cells, but also partially rescued the defects of early endosomes in CapZβ-knockout cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).

claim: Latrunculin A partially rescued the defects of early endosomes in CapZβ-knockout cells.

evidence: The claim is supported by endosome analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: CapZ knockout might increase F-actin density by promoting elongation of pre-existing actin branches to entangle around immature RAB5-positive endocytic vesicles.
source: Therefore, these results suggest that CapZ knockout might increase F-actin density by promoting elongation of pre-existing actin branches to entangle around these immature RAB5-positive endocytic vesicles, and this might impede their fusion and result in the accumulation of small endosomes.

claim: Increased F-actin density might impede fusion of immature RAB5-positive endocytic vesicles and result in the accumulation of small endosomes.
source: Therefore, these results suggest that CapZ knockout might increase F-actin density by promoting elongation of pre-existing actin branches to entangle around these immature RAB5-positive endocytic vesicles, and this might impede their fusion and result in the accumulation of small endosomes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data on F-actin levels and endosome phenotypes.

claim: More RAB5-positive endosomes are in actin-rich regions of the CapZβ-knockout cells than the control cells.
source: We showed that there were more RAB5-positive endosomes in actin-rich regions of the CapZβ-knockout cells than the control cells.

claim: More endosomes were actin-positive in CapZβ-knockout cells when compared to the control cells.

claim: More endosomes sit along the long F-actin in CapZβ-knockout cells than in the control cells.
source: It appeared that more endosomes sit along the long F-actin in CapZβ-knockout cells than in the control cells.

claim: CapZβ knockout significantly increased the colocalization of RAB5 with Arp2/3.
source: We showed that CapZβ knockout significantly increased the colocalization of RAB5 with Arp2/3 (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization analysis data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: More RAB5 puncta were associated with Arp2/3 puncta in CapZβ-knockout cells than in the control cells.

claim: CapZβ knockout markedly increased the colocalization of N-WASP with RAB5.
source: Likewise, CapZβ knockout markedly increased the colocalization of N-WASP with RAB5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1I).

claim: More F-actins are entangled with early endosomes in CapZβ-knockout cells when compared to the control cells.

source: In control cells, RAB5-positive vesicles rapidly moved away from the plasma membrane toward the perinuclear area and fused with each other (left panel in Figure 3F and Figure 3—video 3).

claim: The increased F-actin density around the immature early endosome in CapZβ-knockout cells might act as the physical barrier to impede endosomal trafficking.

claim: CK-636 treatment could lower the F-actins entangled with early endosomes.

claim: CK-636 decreased the number of early endosomes in control cells.

claim: Colocalization between endogenous RAB5 and endogenous ARPC1B in ARP2-knockout cells was markedly weaker than in control cells.

claim: ARP2 knockout decreases the F-actin density around early endosomes.
